source_quote: Cold-adapted breeds still exhibited moderate atopic prevalence.
Large cold-tolerant working breeds had sustained hip dysplasia burden.
Heat-tolerant populations in endemic zones showed increased exposure-linked morbidity.
Heat-adapted dogs showed higher chronic GI parasitism prevalence.
Heat-sensitive breeds demonstrated significantly higher heat stress incidence.
Heat exposure amplified upper-airway morbidity in heat-sensitive dogs.
Temperate cohorts showed stable otitis prevalence.
Dental disease remained a common diagnosis in temperate companion populations.
Cold-adapted spitz lineages had measurable immune-mediated skin disease prevalence.
Temperate urban cohorts showed persistent obesity prevalence.
